scenes.title: What is Event Streaming?
scenes.subtitle: Capturing data as a continuous flow of events
scenes.narration: Event streaming is the practice of capturing data as a continuous, ordered flow of events rather than as periodic snapshots.

scenes.title: The Core Ideas
bullets: An event is an immutable record of something that happened
Events are appended to a log in the order they occur
Consumers react to events in near real time
The stream is unbounded and never truly ends
scenes.narration: An event is an immutable record of something that happened, such as a click, a payment, or a sensor reading. Events are appended to a log in the exact order they occur, which preserves history. Consumers read from that log and react in near real time instead of waiting for a nightly batch. Because new events keep arriving, the stream is unbounded and conceptually never ends.

scenes.title: Batch vs Streaming
scenes.narration: In the traditional batch model, data is generated continuously but collected over hours, then processed in a single large job. By the time results appear, they can already be stale. Streaming closes that gap by processing each event as it arrives, so insights stay fresh.

scenes.title: Batch vs Stream Processing
scenes.narration: Batch processing works on bounded datasets and tolerates high latency, making it ideal for periodic reports. Streaming works on unbounded data with very low latency, which suits fraud detection, live dashboards, and instant notifications. Most modern platforms use both, choosing the right tool for each workload.

scenes.text: Event streaming treats data as an ongoing flow, letting systems react to what is happening right now rather than what happened yesterday.
scenes.narration: The key takeaway is that event streaming treats data as an ongoing flow, letting systems react to what is happening right now rather than what happened yesterday.
